cases.name: Kristil Grimsrud Krug
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Kristil Grimsrud (Krug) was a remarkable soul who touched the lives of those around her with her passion for the performing arts, modern dance, and an exceptional intellect in the sciences. Born on November 24th, 1980, in Boulder, Colorado, Kristil's love for the arts and sciences was evident from an early age. Her love and talent in modern dance were exceptional, and she graced many stages with her beautiful performances.

Kristil’s three children (14, 11, and 8) were the light of her life, and she devoted all her spare energy and resources to their happiness and interests.  She imparted her passion for the performing arts on her daughters, and encouraged her young son’s fascination with technology.

In addition to her artistic pursuits, Kristil possessed an extraordinary mind for the sciences. Recognizing her academic brilliance, she was awarded an Academic Scholarship to the prestigious Colorado School of Mines, where she initially pursued her passion for biochemical engineering. Later, she transferred to the University of Colorado (Boulder), where she continued to excel, graduating with a Bachelor of Science degree in Biochemical Engineering.

Kristil's academic achievements opened doors to a fulfilling career in the field of technology and innovation. She joined Agilent Technologies, where her technical abilities and dedication to her work made her an invaluable member of the team. Agilent Management remembers, “She was such a valuable member of our Project Management team and we will miss her greatly.  She was always a bright spot of creative energy to bring people together and drive to great outcomes.” Her contributions to the company over the past 19 years were not only substantial, but reflective of her commitment to excellence and perseverance in everything she pursued.

Beyond her professional accomplishments, Kristil was known for her kindness, generosity, and infectious laughter. She had an innate ability to inspire those around her, and her warm spirit created a sense of camaraderie wherever she went.

Tragically, Kristil's promising journey was cut short by a senseless act of violence that took her from us too soon. Our hearts are broken and we will miss her dearly. As we grieve the loss of a vibrant and talented soul, we remember Kristil for the joy she brought into our lives, the beauty she shared through her art, and the intellect she brought to the scientific community.

She is remembered by all as successful, driven, loving, considerate, passionate, intelligent, beautiful, and delightful to be around. She accomplished so much in her short life, and had so much left to contribute before being so savagely removed. The world will miss what she had yet to give us."
cases.narrative: On 12/14/2023, she was found deceased during a welfare check. He reportedly spent weeks impersonating her ex-boyfriend and stalking her before killing her. While performing a welfare check, police found her in the garage with a “substantial wound” near her right temple. Preliminary information from her autopsy shows that she sustained two or more blunt-force trauma wounds on the back of her head and one stab wound on the left side of her chest. According to the Adams and Broomfield District Attorney's press release, Kristil had just returned home after getting her children ready for school and dropping them off. As she entered the garage shortly before 8:00 a.m., her husband, Daniel Krug, was lying in wait. He ambushed Kristil from behind, striking her in the head multiple times with a blunt object before fatally stabbing her in the heart.
